all.description: When true, returns all available sports. When false or omitted, returns only recently updated (in-season) sports.

function.name: v4_sports_sport_odds
function.description: Retrieves live and upcoming games with bookmaker odds for a specified sport or across all sports. Returns game details including bookmaker-specific odds formatted by market type. Use this function to get real-time betting data from supported regions and bookmakers.

sport.description: Sport key identifying the sport to query (e.g., 'basketball_nba'). Use 'upcoming' to retrieve the next 8 upcoming games across all sports. Sport keys must match those returned by the /sports endpoint.

regions.description: Comma-separated list of regions to filter bookmakers (e.g., 'us,uk'). Each region will count as 1 request against your API quota. See documentation for region-bookmaker mappings.

oddsformat.description: Format for returned odds values. Select a standardized odds format.

markets.description: Comma-separated list of odds markets to include (e.g., 'h2h,outrights'). Each market will count as 1 request against your API quota. Common markets include 'h2h' (head-to-head), 'spreads', and 'totals'.

dateformat.description: Format for returned timestamps in game data.

function.name: v4_sports_sport_scores
function.description: Retrieves live, upcoming, and optionally recent completed games with scores for a specified sport. Currently in beta for select sports; refer to the [sports list](https://the-odds-api.com/sports-odds-data/sports-apis.html) for available options.

sport.description: Sport key identifying the specific sport to retrieve game data for. Must match a supported sport key from the API's available sports list.

daysfrom.description: Optional number of days in the past (valid values: 1-3) to include completed games in the response. If omitted, only live and upcoming games are included.

function.name: calculate_etf
function.description: Calculates the theoretical equity asset percentage change for a leveraged ETF based on its leverage factor and the underlying asset's percentage change. This function is useful for financial analysis of leveraged investment products.

leverage.description: The ETF's leverage factor relative to the underlying asset (e.g., 2 for 2x leverage, 3 for 3x leverage). This determines how strongly the ETF responds to the underlying asset's movements.

underlying.description: The percentage change of the underlying asset as a whole number (e.g., 5 for 5%, -2 for -2%). This represents the base asset's performance before applying leverage.

function.name: leveraged_equity_calculator
function.description: Calculates the projected equity value after a price change for a leveraged investment. This function helps analyze leveraged ETF performance by quantifying the impact of leverage on equity growth or decline based on underlying asset price movements.

leverage.description: The leverage multiplier applied to the investment. For example, 2 for 2x leverage. Higher values amplify both gains and losses.

originalshareprice.description: The initial price of the underlying asset before the price change. Must be a positive integer.

originalequity.description: The initial investment amount at the start of the period. Must be a positive integer.

projectedshareprice.description: The expected future price of the underlying asset. Must be a positive integer.

function.description: Retrieves the current average exchange rates for Tunisian Dinar (TND) against US Dollar (USD) and Euro (EUR). function.name: get_laws_for_one_state
function.description: Retrieves gun law documentation links for a specific U.S. state using the provided RapidAPI key.

statename.description: The name of the state for which to retrieve gun law documentation.

function.name: getgamecontent
function.description: Fetches the content of a specific NHL game using its game ID.

is_id.description: The ID of the game. The first 4 digits identify the season of the game (e.g., 2017 for the 2017-2018 season). The next 2 digits indicate the type of game (01 = preseason, 02 = regular season, 03 = playoffs, 04 = all-star). The final 4 digits identify the specific game number. For regular season and preseason games, this ranges from 0001 to the number of games played. For playoff games, the 2nd digit of the specific number gives the round of the playoffs, the 3rd digit specifies the matchup, and the 4th digit specifies the game (out of 7).

function.name: search_image
function.description: Performs an image search using the Google Search JSON API and returns a JSON response containing information about images that match the search query.

q.description: The search query for finding images.

num.description: Number of search results to return. Valid values are between 1 and 20, inclusive. Default is 10.

lr.description: Restricts the search to documents written in a particular language. Default is 'lang_en'.

start.description: The index of the first result to return. Default is 0.

gl.description: A two-letter country code that boosts search results whose country of origin matches the parameter value. Default is 'US'.

language.description: ISO 639-1 language code for the response content (e.g., 'en' for English, 'zh' for Chinese). Determines the language of catalog metadata and product descriptions.

function.name: get_item_review
function.description: Retrieves product reviews from JD.com for a specific item, including customer ratings, feedback text, and metadata. Useful for analyzing product performance, customer satisfaction, and market reception.

itemid.description: Unique identifier of the product on JD.com (e.g., SKU number or product ID). Required to fetch reviews for a specific item.

framesize.description: Number of reviews to return per request (frame size). Controls pagination size for large review datasets.

language.description: Language code for filtering reviews (e.g., 'en' for English, 'zh' for Chinese). Returns reviews in the specified language if available.

frameposition.description: Page number of reviews to fetch. Used in conjunction with framesize for paginating through multiple sets of reviews.

function.name: get_vendor
function.description: Retrieves detailed information about a JD.com seller account, including vendor profile, store details, and product offerings. Useful for product research, vendor analysis, and marketplace operations.

language.description: Language code for response localization (e.g., 'en' for English, 'zh' for Chinese).

vendorid.description: Unique identifier for the JD seller account. When omitted, the API may return information for the default vendor context or all vendors.

function.name: search_for_items
function.description: Searches JD.com's product database with advanced filtering and sorting capabilities. Supports queries by keyword, price range, category, order volume, and image similarity. Ideal for product discovery, competitive analysis, or inventory monitoring.

frameposition.description: Starting position for pagination (zero-indexed). Use with framesize to implement page-based navigation.

language.description: Language code for search results (ISO 639-1 format). Determines language of product descriptions and metadata.

framesize.description: Number of items to return per page. Must be between 1 and 100.

imageurl.description: URL of reference image for visual similarity search. Leave empty for text-based search only.

minprice.description: Minimum product price filter (inclusive). Set to 0 to remove lower price limit.

itemtitle.description: Search query term for product title matching. Supports partial matches and fuzzy search.

minvolume.description: Minimum order volume filter (inclusive). Set to 0 to ignore order volume.

maxprice.description: Maximum product price filter (inclusive). Set to -1 to remove upper price limit.

categoryid.description: Restrict results to specific category ID. Leave empty for cross-category search.

orderby.description: Sort criteria for results. Available options: 'price_asc', 'price_desc', 'volume_desc', 'relevance'

function.name: get_race
function.description: Retrieves detailed race results and classification data for cycling competitions. Returns information about race winners, standings, and category-specific classifications. Use this function to analyze race outcomes or obtain historical performance data.

racecategory.description: Race category (e.g., Grand Tour, Classic, Stage Race) - valid values can be obtained from the GET Races endpoint. This defines the classification structure and race type.

race.description: Identifier for the specific race within the category (e.g., 'Tour de France', 'Giro d'Italia'). Must be a valid race name for the specified category.

afterstage.description: Stage number after which to retrieve classification data. Valid values are positive integers up to the total number of stages in the race. Omitting returns overall classification.

year.description: Year of the race (e.g., '2023'). If not specified, defaults to the current year.

classification.description: Type of classification data to retrieve. Valid options include GC (General Classification), Points, KOM (King of Mountains), Youth, Teams, and Stage.

function.name: get_races
function.description: Retrieves UCI cycling races based on category and year. Returns comprehensive race data including dates, locations, classifications, and event details.

category.description: Race category filter to specify type of events (e.g., professional tours, championships, regional circuits)

year.description: Filter races by calendar year (4-digit format, e.g., '2023'). When omitted, defaults to current year data.

function.name: get_riders
function.description: Retrieves comprehensive cyclist data from the Union Cycliste Internationale (UCI) database, including professional riders, their career statistics, and team affiliations. Useful for sports analytics, historical research, and cycling enthusiast applications.

year.description: Optional four-digit year (e.g., '2023') to filter cyclists active during a specific season. When omitted, returns cyclists across all available historical records.

function.name: get_teams
function.description: Retrieves comprehensive data about all UCI-registered professional cycling teams for a specified season. Returns team details including names, riders, performance statistics, and classification information. Useful for sports analytics, team comparisons, and historical cycling data research.

year.description: Season year to retrieve data for, formatted as 'YYYY'. If not specified, defaults to current season data.

messages.content: Thank you for the information! Could you clarify when Chicago and Winnipeg will align with Mexico City's UTC-05:00 offset during daylight saving? I’d like to plan potential side trips to art museums in these cities without time zone conflicts. Additionally, are there any other major cities in the Americas with a permanent UTC-05:00 offset (no DST adjustments)? This would help me avoid scheduling disruptions for future travels.

To address your questions:

### **1. Chicago and Winnipeg's Alignment with Mexico City (UTC-05:00):**
- **Overlap Period:** Both cities align with Mexico City's UTC-05:00 offset **during their overlapping daylight saving time (DST) periods**.  
  - **Chicago (USA):**  
    - DST starts on the **second Sunday in March** (e.g., March 10, 2024).  
    - DST ends on the **first Sunday in November** (e.g., November 3, 2024).  
  - **Mexico City (Mexico):**  
    - DST starts on the **first Sunday in April** (e.g., April 7, 2024).  
    - DST ends on the **last Sunday in October** (e.g., October 27, 2024).  
  - **Overlap:** From **April 7 to October 27** (UTC-05:00 for both).  
  - **Non-Overlap:**  
    - March 10–April 7: Chicago is UTC-05:00, Mexico City is UTC-06:00.  
    - October 27–November 3: Mexico City reverts to UTC-06:00, Chicago remains UTC-05:00.  

- **Winnipeg (Canada):**  
  - Follows the same DST schedule as Chicago (second Sunday in March to first Sunday in November).  
  - Aligns with Mexico City from **April 7 to October 27** (UTC-05:00).  

For art museum planning, prioritize visits during the overlap period (April–October) to avoid time zone conflicts.

---

### **2. Major Cities in the Americas with Permanent UTC-05:00 (No DST):**  
These cities **do not observe DST**, remaining on UTC-05:00 year-round:  
- **Kingston, Jamaica**  
- **Bogotá, Colombia**  
- **Lima, Peru**  
- **Quito, Ecuador** (mainland; Galápagos Islands are UTC-06:00)  
- **Cayman Islands**  
- **Turks and Caicos Islands** (observes DST only for 1 week in October; negligible impact)  
- **Port-au-Prince, Haiti** (does not observe DST consistently; confirm annually)  

**Note:**  
- **Indiana (USA):** Most of Indiana observes Eastern Time (UTC-05:00) and **does not** observe DST (e.g., Indianapolis). However, 12 counties in northwest and southwest Indiana **do** observe DST (UTC-04:00 in summer).

function.name: channel
function.description: Retrieves comprehensive channel information including metadata, content details, and associated videos. This function is useful for channel analysis, content management, or data collection purposes when working with media platforms like YouTube.

is_id.description: The unique identifier of the channel (e.g., a YouTube channel ID like 'UCN9Nj4tjXbVTLYWN0EKly_Q'). This ID is typically found in channel URLs or API responses.

function.name: comments
function.description: Retrieves comments from a video. Use this function to fetch user comments sorted by popularity or recency. Returns a list of comments with author, content, and engagement metrics.

is_id.description: The unique identifier of the video for which to retrieve comments. This is typically found in the video's URL (e.g., 'dQw4w9WgXcQ' in 'https://youtu.be/dQw4w9WgXcQ').

sort_by.description: Determines the order of comments. Set to 'top' to prioritize comments with the highest engagement (upvotes), or 'new' to show the most recent comments first.

function.name: playlist
function.description: Retrieves detailed information about a YouTube playlist using its unique identifier. This function provides access to playlist metadata including title, description, items, and other relevant details.

is_id.description: The unique identifier of the YouTube playlist (e.g., 'PLV3BLrRejJR_8Xrbev1_7RjIZTg1qb'). This ID can be extracted from the playlist URL (e.g., 'https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=ID_HERE').

function.name: popular
function.description: Retrieves trending videos from YouTube's popular section. This function provides access to a curated list of highly-viewed videos across all categories, sorted by engagement metrics. Returns key video details such as titles, view counts, and publication dates. Use this to discover currently viral content or top-performing videos without specific filtering criteria.

function.name: search_suggestions
function.description: Generates search suggestions based on partial query input, similar to YouTube's autocomplete feature. Useful for enhancing user search experiences by providing relevant suggestions as users type. Example: '/search/suggestions?q=crypto' would return related terms like 'cryptocurrency news', 'crypto prices', or 'crypto mining tutorials'.

q.description: The search query string to generate suggestions for. Should be a partial or complete search term (e.g., 'crypto', 'machine learning tutorial'). This parameter directly influences the relevance of the suggestions returned.

function.name: trending_music_gaming_news_movies
function.description: Retrieves trending videos data filtered by category and region. Supports retrieving trending content in music, gaming, news, and movies categories with regional specificity using ISO 3166 country codes.

type.description: Content category filter for trending videos. Valid values include music, gaming, news, and movies. If omitted, returns trending videos across all categories.

region.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code for regional trending results (e.g., 'US' for United States, 'GB' for United Kingdom). Defaults to 'US' when unspecified.

function.name: video
function.description: Retrieves comprehensive metadata about a YouTube video, including title, description, upload date, duration, view count, and other statistics. This function is useful for content verification, video analysis, or programmatic access to YouTube video details.

is_id.description: The unique identifier of the YouTube video. This is typically an 11-character alphanumeric string found in the video's URL (e.g., 'dQw4w9WgXcQ' in 'https://youtu.be/dQw4w9WgXcQ').
